output.summary: An annual flowering plant native to Mexico and Guatemala and naturalised in many other countries. Its many cultivars have velvet-textured yellow, orange or russet flowers. In Georgian cuisine, the dried, ground petals are a pungent, earthy spice known as Imeretian saffron.
output.edibilityNote: Dried, ground petals are used as a spice in Georgian cuisine; florets can also colour human foods.
